scope: PS2 China 24x24 verified Han versus recovered historical BDF and selected original PCF/HBF sources

method.common_repertoire: same Unicode scalar, U+4E00..U+9FFF, within the verified PS2 Han mapping
method.exact_full_bitmap: same BBX bitmap width, height and all pixels, including whitespace; no padding, shift or resize
method.exact_cropped_ink: remove only each bitmap's empty outer rows and columns, then require identical dimensions and every pixel
method.metrics: BBX x/y offsets and runtime baselines/advances are not compared; PS2 runtime metrics are unknown
method.restrictions: no scaling, stroke normalization, substitutions, Unicode normalization or outline rasterization
method.zero_common: not a comparison; excluded from highest-rate calculation
method.interpretation: low exact-match rates do not prove originality, hand drawing, design independence, ancestry or licensing

limitations: The 221 BDF containers are not 221 proven-complete original fonts; some contain only a limited mapped subset.
211 restored BDF files contain comparable mapped Han. Zero common Han is not a negative match result.
ccic_taipeil24 had no Unicode assignments in the converted BDF; its original Big5 BDF supplies 13,061 comparable Han, all different.
Taipei original Big5 names include alternate codes for U+5341 and U+5345. Accepting any original variant does not change any PS2 comparison count.
Historical reference coverage remains incomplete. Low exact-match rates do not establish originality, manual pixel design, independence or copyright status.
The comparison concerns pixels, not unknown PS2 runtime baseline or advance metrics.
The largest overlap is 939 of 6,763 common Han (13.884371%), not an almost-identical full-library duplicate. Partial overlap is still substantive evidence to retain.
